chunk-001:c001.proposition: Current origin-of-life claims exceed the available chemical evidence and give students and professors an unjustified impression that major explanatory steps have been solved.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Small laboratory experiments do not warrant confidence in a primordial-soup-to-cell account unless evidence connects the demonstrated chemistry to the emergence of the first cell.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Evidence that early Earth contained small molecules does not establish that a prebiotic mixture progressed from those starting materials to cells and life.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: An origin-of-life explanation must account for both information and the complex material organization of a cell, because recursive information alone does not constitute life.

chunk-002:c002-01.proposition: The engineered molybdate system demonstrates an autocatalytic templating reaction, but that result remains far from demonstrating a transition to biological life.

chunk-002:c002-04.proposition: Public-facing origin-of-life explanations can create confident impressions that are not sustained when the technical details supporting those explanations are requested.

chunk-002:c002-05.proposition: Origin-of-life experiments cannot support broad extrapolations while leaving unresolved the synthesis, purification, and integration needed to carry products through subsequent functional steps.

chunk-002:c002-09.proposition: As cellular organization and communication become better understood, the explanatory target grows more complex, leaving simple information-generating chemistry far from biological life.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-01.proposition: Origin-of-life research needs explicit and demanding shared criteria for deciding when a chemical system genuinely begins to qualify as life rather than merely appearing lifelike.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-03.proposition: A credible claim of self-replication must address copying fidelity and continued replication rather than merely producing one copy before the system fails.
